q-35169.name: Question 1
q-35169.problem: Given that the function $f(x)$ has an inverse ${f}^{-1}(x)$, and the point $(2,-1)$ lies on the graph $y=f(x),$ which point must lie on the graph of $y={f}^{-1}(x)?$
q-35169.worked_solution:
The function $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ is a reflection of $y=f(x)$ in the line $y=x.$ Therefore, each point $(a,b)$ on $y=f(x)$ has a corresponding point $(b,a)$ on $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ (the $x$ and $y$ coordinates swap).

Since the point $(2,-1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ the point $(-1,2)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

q-35169.html:
Question 1
?

Given that the function f(x) has an inverse f−1(x), and the point (2,−1) lies on the graph y=f(x), which point must lie on the graph of y=f−1(x)?

a
(2,−1)
b
(2,1)
c
(1,2)
d
(−1,2)
e
(1,−2)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function y=f−1(x) is a reflection of y=f(x) in the line y=x. Therefore, each point (a,b) on y=f(x) has a corresponding point (b,a) on y=f−1(x) (the x and y coordinates swap).

Since the point (2,−1) lies on y=f(x), the point (−1,2) lies on y=f−1(x).

q-35178.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14228361/assets/2280a258ec2cf548a5393772e497bece3ecbb61549c0d7260bad2146a9f3a094.png)

The graph of $f(x)$ is given above. Which of the following could be the graph of ${f}^{-1}(x)?$
q-35178.worked_solution:
The function $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ is a reflection of $y=f(x)$ in the line $y=x.$ Of the given options, the only graph satisfying this condition is the one shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14228361/assets/b2f729211c24879686601523f74935332dccbd6bf2e89b63af794b70dc721b1d.png)

Notice that the points on $y=f(x)$ have corresponding points on $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ with the coordinates swapped.

$$
\begin{aligned}(1,3) & ⟶(3,1) \\ (\sqrt{3},9) & ⟶(9,\sqrt{3})\end{aligned}
$$
